Extract Raster Values by Polygon

Source: R/extract_cell_by_poly.R
extract_cell_by_poly.Rd

This function extracts the values of every raster cell within each polygon, with the fraction of the cell inside the polygon, using the exactextractr package on the terra raster directly.

Usage

extract_cell_by_poly(
  raster,
  poly,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  chunk = "auto",
  ...
)

Arguments

raster

A SpatRaster representing the raster data to extract.

poly

A SpatVector or sf object representing the polygon(s) for extraction.

id

Optional name of the column of poly identifying the polygons. The result's identifier column takes this name. Default ID_adm_div.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

chunk

"auto" extracts in blocks of layers only when needed; a whole number forces that many layers per block; FALSE never splits.

...

additional arguments to pass to exactextractr::exact_extract.

Value

A c4e_tbl with the polygon identifier, the cell coordinates (x_cell, y_cell), the coverage_fraction and one column per layer.

Details

Each cell is identified by the polygon it belongs to and its centre. The polygon identifier is the polygon's own ID_adm_div (or the column named by id) when it has one, else its row number. The result is a c4e_tbl carrying the raster's context, ready for cell-level indicators that are later aggregated with the coverage fractions.

When the result would exceed the memory budget (see ?c4e), the layers are extracted in blocks and bound together.

See also

exact_extract, extract_by_poly()

Examples

tmax <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
adm_div <- terra::vect(
  system.file("extdata", "adm_div.gpkg", package = "c4e"))

# one row per cell and division, with the share of the cell inside it
extract_cell_by_poly(tmax[[1:3]], adm_div)
#> # A tibble: 39 × 7
#> # Context:  tmax [K], day, wide; key ID_adm_div
#>    ID_adm_div x_cell y_cell coverage_fraction `2021-01-01` `2021-01-02`
#>    <chr>       <dbl>  <dbl>             <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl>
#>  1 1            30.1    0.1                 1         292.         293.
#>  2 1            30.3    0.1                 1         294.         291.
#>  3 1            30.5    0.1                 1         290.         296.
#>  4 1            30.1   -0.1                 1         294.         294.
#>  5 1            30.3   -0.1                 1         293.         295.
#>  6 1            30.5   -0.1                 1         296.         296.
#>  7 1            30.1   -0.3                 1         288.         296.
#>  8 1            30.3   -0.3                 1         293.         293.
#>  9 1            30.5   -0.3                 1         292.         294.
#> 10 1            30.1   -0.5                 1         296.         293.
#> # ℹ 29 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: `2021-01-03` <dbl>
